actions.justification: MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle: Measure serum lactate immediately to assess severity of tissue hypoperfusion. Must be done within 1 hour. Initial lactate guides resuscitation strategy.
MANDATORY per SSC guidelines: Obtain blood cultures BEFORE administering antibiotics to maximize diagnostic yield. Critical for pathogen identification and antibiotic stewardship.

MANDATORY per SSC guidelines: Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour of septic shock recognition. Patient has unknown source — empiric broad-spectrum coverage required immediately after blood cultures obtained.
MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle: administer 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid for hypotension (BP 82/48, MAP 59). This is the primary mandatory action not yet completed.

Patient has persistent hypotension with MAP 59 (<65 mmHg). SSC guidelines recommend norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor in septic shock to target MAP ≥65 mmHg. Should be initiated during/after fluid resuscitation given severity of shock.

Patient has confusion (potential neurologic dysfunction), hypotension, tachycardia, tachypnea, SpO2 91%, and CKD — need to evaluate SOFA score components and degree of multi-organ dysfunction to guide further management.

Patient has abdominal pain as a chief complaint — identifying the infection source (e.g., intra-abdominal, urinary, biliary) is critical to guide targeted therapy and determine if source control is needed. This should be done in parallel with ongoing resuscitation.

Patient has CKD stage 3 and diabetes — BMP is essential to assess renal function (creatinine, BUN), electrolytes, glucose, and bicarbonate (metabolic acidosis in septic shock). Critical for monitoring fluid resuscitation effects and vasopressor titration.

MAP remains at 59 mmHg (below target of ≥65 mmHg) and SpO2 is 91% — serial vital sign assessment is essential to evaluate response to norepinephrine and fluid resuscitation, and to determine if vasopressin augmentation or oxygen supplementation is needed.

Initial lactate was critically elevated at 5.8 mmol/L. SSC guidelines mandate serial lactate measurements to guide resuscitation adequacy. Remeasuring after fluid resuscitation and vasopressor initiation is essential to assess treatment response.

MAP remains at 59 mmHg (below target of 65) despite norepinephrine initiation and 30mL/kg crystalloid. Reassessment of perfusion status is critical to determine if additional vasopressors, fluids, or other interventions are needed.

Patient is in septic shock on vasopressors with labile hemodynamics (MAP 59). An arterial line provides continuous, accurate blood pressure monitoring essential for titrating vasopressor therapy, and facilitates serial blood draws for labs.

Patient has SpO2 of 91% and unknown infection source. Chest X-ray is essential to identify pulmonary source of sepsis (pneumonia, pleural effusion) and assess for pulmonary edema after fluid resuscitation. Critical for source identification.

CBC is needed to assess WBC count (infection severity), hemoglobin (anemia may worsen oxygen delivery with SpO2 91%), and platelet count (DIC screening in septic shock). Essential for ongoing management.

Lactate of 5.8 and septic shock with multi-organ involvement increases risk of DIC. Coagulation studies (PT/INR, PTT, fibrinogen) are needed to screen for coagulopathy and guide transfusion/FFP decisions.

Central venous access is needed for safe vasopressor administration and hemodynamic monitoring. Patient is on norepinephrine and may need additional vasopressors; central line placement is standard of care in septic shock.

MAP remains at 59 mmHg (target ≥65) despite norepinephrine. SSC guidelines recommend adding vasopressin (up to 0.03 units/min) as an adjunct to norepinephrine to achieve MAP target and potentially reduce norepinephrine dose requirements.
Baseline procalcitonin level supports antibiotic stewardship decisions and serial measurements can guide duration of antibiotic therapy per SSC guidelines.

Patient has persistent hypotension (MAP 59, BP 82/48), elevated lactate 5.8, and SpO2 91%. Additional crystalloid fluid bolus is indicated to support ongoing resuscitation despite vasopressors already started, as per SSC guidelines recommending continued fluid resuscitation in septic shock.

MANDATORY action: MAP is 59 mmHg, below target of 65 mmHg. Despite norepinephrine and vasopressin already running, this mandatory bundle element must be formally completed. Vasopressor therapy is indicated per SSC guidelines to maintain MAP ≥ 65 mmHg in septic shock.

Patient has septic shock with lactate 5.8, MAP 59 despite vasopressors, SpO2 91%, and multiple comorbidities (CKD, DM2, HTN). ICU admission is required for continuous hemodynamic monitoring, vasopressor titration, and organ support.
